jurisdiction.publisher: Environment and Climate Change Canada (ECCC) - Water Survey of Canada

domain: hydrology - daily river flow / water level series for Canadian gauging stations
prediction_question: The task this source would support (rejected before construction): predict station-level daily flow exceedance or the next-day/day-ahead flow for Canadian hydrometric stations - the canonical streamflow-forecasting task on Water Survey of Canada / HYDAT data.
prediction_time: Would be stateable (day T observations -> day T+1 outcome) - but the task already exists in ML-ready form, which is the reason for the verdict.
target_definition: Not fixed: flow exceedance vs a datum/threshold, or day-ahead flow. The exact label is moot given the verdict.

split_strategy: Not built. Measured prior art already ships the panel and the splits: CAMELS-SPAT provides 'Streamflow observations, forcing data and geospatial data... for 1426 streamflow measurement stations located across the United States and Canada' (daily and hourly streamflow at basin outlets, 4 meteorological forcings, catchment attributes - FRDR datasets 9ca63670-9e40-477c-a8a8-30f61205d668 / fef15147-940a-4a7d-86c3-373ec7d67ec4, Knoben et al., 'Catchment Attributes and MEteorology for Large-Sample SPATially distributed analysis (CAMELS-SPAT)', doi:10.5194/egusphere-2025-893), and HYSETS ('Hydrometeorological Sandbox - École de Technologie Supérieure', Arsenault et al., Earth System Science Data 2020) covers 14,000+ North American basins including Canada with daily streamflow and forcings.

measurements.mirror_evidence: Web search 2026-10-21 (queries recorded in notes.md): CAMELS-SPAT explicitly ships Canadian-station daily/hourly streamflow with forcings and static catchment attributes in a research dataset designed for ML (papers already benchmark LSTM streamflow models on it, e.g. Kratzert et al. line of work extended to CAMELS-SPAT in a 2025 preprint evaluating across 921 North American catchments); HYSETS ships the same for Canadian basins. A Scout-built Canadian streamflow task would repackage data a consumer can already download with splits and a scored contract only one step removed - the exact mirror case the standing novelty rule refuses. The canonical task is also already represented in this bench's own family (malaysia-river-danger-exceedance, live), so a Canadian twin would duplicate the family as well as the public prior art.
measurements.cost_note: Extraction cost was deliberately NOT measured: CAMELS-SPAT has already paid it for the Canadian stations, which is precisely why this is a mirror and not a candidate. Catalogue identity was measured (5 CKAN records read back anonymously).

rejection_reason: REJECTED as a mirror: the prediction task this source would carry (Canadian station-level streamflow forecasting / flow exceedance) already exists in public ML-ready form - CAMELS-SPAT (1,426 US+Canada basins, daily+hourly streamflow, 4 forcing sets, catchment attributes; FRDR, Knoben et al. 2025) and HYSETS (Arsenault et al., ESSD 2020) - and is a live family in this bench (malaysia-river-danger-exceedance). Publishing a HYDAT derivative would ship nothing the consumer cannot already download. Novelty check recorded via check-novelty.py with verdict 'mirror'.
next_action: Dropped. Do not re-open while CAMELS-SPAT and HYSETS remain downloadable. A genuinely different formulation (e.g. real-time flood-warning verification against ECCC's own issued warnings - a warnings-outcome task rather than a flow-forecast task) would have to be argued as a NEW candidate with its own novelty check, not as a reopening of this one.

novelty_check.method: public catalogue search (Hugging Face datasets, Zenodo, arXiv) plus web search for an existing ML-ready formulation of this exact task
